texts.text:
The clearing has not emptied. The assembly lingers in uneven rings, their Weave-Script flickering with the weight of what they just witnessed.

Seren remains kneeling at the center, composed, her aqua skin catching the last light. The presiding Dohkar steps forward.

THE PRESIDING DOHKAR: "This rite is mine to preside, and what the Sacrificiant did in it is mine to rule on."

His voice carries without effort. The assembly straightens around him.

THE PRESIDING DOHKAR: "In a preliminary review, before this assembly."

The words land like a seal pressed into wax. My standing, the path my father walked, shifts visibly in the eyes of every witness.

Julian has not moved from the edge, yet the assembly has already made room for him.

His stillness is the only thing that can make the Dohkar's gaze sharpen.

THE PRESIDING DOHKAR: "The review will be recorded. The Sacrificiant will answer for her conduct."

The assembly's attention tightens around me. Seren's mother is still on her feet.

Julian's gaze finds mine across the clearing. He does not speak, but the room has already adjusted to his presence.

The Dohkar's Weave-Script flares hard and flat.

THE PRESIDING DOHKAR: "This will be settled before witnesses. The record will stand."

My standing fractures in the open air. The path I never imagined not walking narrows to a single recorded line.

Julian's presence changes what the room believes is possible. The Dohkar notices.

The deck is still in my hand. The gold edges catch the failing light.

One of the heavy gold cards slips out.

I realize that old tarot deck is still in my hand. Reassuringly solid. Present. One of the heavy gold cards slips out — “Petition Fate” is inscribed in it.

I slide my fingers over the scarred wrist still holding mine.

The Dohkar's words still hang over the clearing.

I need the review to pass without stripping what I still hold.

Let the review pass without stripping what I still hold.

One crimson blade bends sharply toward my hand, then straightens.

Coincidence. It has to be.

Julian's hand stays where it is.

The Answer still rests between us.

JULIAN: The Answer will take the memory of the one you lost.

The words land like a seal pressed into wax.

That memory is the only thing left of what I lost.

The deck is still in my free hand.

JULIAN: You cannot withhold it during the review.

His stillness makes the clearing feel smaller.

The Dohkar's ruling has already begun to narrow what I can keep.

My fingers stay on the scar.

If I let go now the price will still be taken.

The assembly lingers behind us, watching.

Julian's gaze does not waver.

The deck edges catch the last light.

I realize the deck is still in my hand. As I slide Petition Fate back in, I notice a flash of red in the otherwise gold stack. “Tempt Fate.” Great-grandma never let me play with that one. A sword raised to a blood-red sky, lightning arcing down from the clouds (or maybe arcing up?) Ow! Static shock reminds me I need to pay attention to the present…

I step back. The Answer leaves my hands.

The Dohkar's voice cuts across the clearing.

PRESIDING DOHKAR: "The Provast demanded this review."

The words land while the grass still holds the warmth of the rite.

PRESIDING DOHKAR: "While it runs you will not leave the grounds."

Seren's hands stay folded in her lap.

PRESIDING DOHKAR: "You will not speak of the rite."

The second restriction settles between my ribs.

PRESIDING DOHKAR: "And you will surrender The Answer to his keeping."

Julian has not moved.

The assembly watches the space between us.

JULIAN: "Agreed."

His voice carries no triumph.

Only the weight of what he has set in motion.

I feel the choice form before the Dohkar finishes speaking.

Accept the restrictions with his name on record.

Or contest his role before the assembly can disperse.

Either path leaves the review in motion.

Julian's stillness makes the clearing feel smaller.

The Dohkar waits.

My fingers close harder around The Answer.

The clearing holds its breath.

Seren remains kneeling, small hands folded.

The Presiding Dohkar watches without moving.

Julian has not shifted from his place at the edge.

The assembly's eyes rest on the space between us.

My grip stays firm on The Answer.

The Dohkar's silence stretches.

I feel the weight of every gaze.

Julian's stillness pulls the clearing inward.

The Answer warms under my palms.

The Dohkar's eyes narrow.

Julian speaks.

JULIAN: "The record of the rite alone will stand before the Chayr."

His voice carries no challenge.

Only the clean line of what he permits.

The Dohkar inclines his head once.

The assembly shifts.

Questions that might have reached deeper fall away.

My hands remain on The Answer.

The review now sits inside the boundary he drew.

Seren watches me.

The Dohkar waits for my answer.

Julian has not looked away.

The narrowed scope stands between me and every question that could reach further.

Accept it and keep what remains, or speak against the line he has drawn.

oas.pcSay: I shaped nothing. Ask me properly.
oas.pcSayRaw: I shaped nothing. Ask me properly.
oas.liDialogue: You shaped the rite with every tilt of your gaze toward me. Did you call my name hoping I would step forward and claim the moment as yours?
oas.liAction: Julian's scarred fingers stay closed over mine on the double-ended shaft.

oas.pcDo: I stand still, the tension thickening the air between us.
oas.pcDoRaw: Stand still, letting the tension fill the air
oas.liDialogue: Your breath betrays the call you sent. You shaped the rite with every glance toward me, hoping I would step forward and claim the moment as yours.
oas.liAction: Julian's scarred fingers press the Answer deeper into my palm.

oas.pcSay: I will not answer your questions in this place, not in this way.
oas.pcDo: I step back, drawing my hand from his grip on the shaft.
oas.pcSayRaw: I won't answer your questions here, not like this.
oas.pcDoRaw: Step back, pulling my hand away from his grip
oas.liDialogue: The Answer will reveal itself regardless of your choice. Your retreat alters nothing.
oas.liAction: Julian's weathered hand lingers in the air for a heartbeat after letting go.

oas.pcDo: I stand still, letting the tension fill the air between us.

oas.liDialogue: Each look you cast my way during the ceremony resonated more than any spoken vow. Did you think I’d stride in and seize the occasion?

oas.liDialogue: The truth rests weighty in your palm. Your quiet pulls all attention nearer.
